extracted.intended_audience: mathematics education researchers, university mathematics faculty, and graduate student support staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practical recommendations for supporting the academic transition of mathematics graduate students and for designing/using criterion-referenced assessment (CRA) so it aids learning and grading transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of CRA for graders
rubrics_metrics.description: CRA sheets provided better guidance as to what was expected for different grade levels/marks and made the process of allocating scores by graders much clearer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRA can make grading procedures more transparent to graders; criteria should be written to explicitly indicate the types of judgments graders will use when assessing student work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit student instruction on CRA use
rubrics_metrics.description: Students and graders need to be explicitly informed exactly why they are provided with criteria and how they can be used to assist learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate to students how criteria guide response attempts, what graders deem 'important', and how to use criteria both during assessment and when reviewing graded work so that criteria translate into improved learning practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRA as a tool for post-feedback reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: A small percentage of students indicated they did refer to the criteria sheets after the tasks were graded in order to get a different, higher level representation of where they had made errors in their responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage and instruct students to use CRA sheets after grading to identify error patterns and guide remediation; make the relationship between criteria and common errors explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and wording of criteria and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The criteria and standards must be carefully designed and worded so that they are exactly the types of judgments the grader is using while assessing students’ work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction of criteria/standards is not straightforward — require careful phrasing to align student-facing descriptors with actual grader judgments; involve examples and exemplar responses to reduce ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance and training for academic staff in CRA development
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic staff need to be closely guided in the development of these elements of any criterion referenced assessment strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide staff development and explicit guidance materials for graders and instructors to ensure consistent construction and application of CRA criteria and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRA is not sufficient alone to support learning
rubrics_metrics.description: CRA may be useful in raising student awareness about the assessment process, it is not sufficient in itself as the assessment method of choice to support students in the learning process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement CRA with instruction on how to use feedback, scaffolding for applying criteria, and other formative approaches; do not assume merely providing criteria will change student learning behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate students on how to use feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be more important to educate students regarding 'how' to use feedback at all as a way to assist in their learning process, rather than to rely solely on the method itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach explicit strategies for interpreting criteria-aligned feedback, planning improvements, and applying feedback to future assessments; integrate this into course activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider graders' perceptions of CRA usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should consider the impact on graders/academics and the usefulness they perceive in employing criterion referenced assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and use grader feedback on CRA clarity, workload, and perceived fairness to iterate on criteria design and implementation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide comprehensive administrative information to new graduate students
rubrics_metrics.description: Students wished they had more information regarding issues ranging from tuition costs to teaching responsibilities, from paychecks to degree requirements, from health insurance to the amount of time and effort a doctoral program would require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departments should proactively provide clear, easily accessible information about administrative, financial, and programmatic expectations early (orientation/advising) to reduce uncertainty and help students plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early communication of research expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Several students wished that the idea of research, an explanation of the procedures and types of work involved, and the length and depth required by the research process had been introduced earlier in their degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce what research entails (types of work, timeline, advisor role) early in graduate programs so students can make informed decisions about pursuing a Ph.D. versus a master’s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring to ease transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Students felt that a mentoring program for graduate students would have helped them with their transition to graduate school (e.g., matching a new grad student with an older graduate student and possibly a professor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement formal or informal mentoring structures (peer mentors, faculty mentors) to provide social, academic, and navigational support during early graduate study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster community and study-group structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Students emphasized the role of community in supporting academic work and providing emotional/social support; study groups helped with understanding material and camaraderie ('Yay! We're all in this together').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage formation of study groups, collaborative tasks, and peer networks early in programs to provide both academic scaffolding and social support; recognize community-building as central to persistence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address competition and its effects on support networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition (real or perceived) affected students' ability to form supportive study groups; in some classes grading practices amplified competitiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of assessment and classroom practices that create zero-sum competitions; design environments and assessments that encourage cooperation where appropriate and clarify grading practices to reduce destructive competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty approachability and relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Students reported that some professors were less approachable and that adjusting to new faculty and teaching styles impacted their transition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote faculty behaviors and departmental policies that increase accessibility (office hours, approachable mentoring, orientation to teaching styles) so students can seek help when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide preparatory 'bridge' resources for under-prepared content
rubrics_metrics.description: Students compensated for specific prior knowledge deficiencies in areas like topology, linear algebra, and complex analysis; some suggested departmental review or preparatory resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer bridge courses, review manuals, recommended reading lists, or preparatory workshops to help incoming students strengthen gaps in prerequisite knowledge before advanced sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify seminar expectations and advisor-finding processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Students were surprised at seminar culture, expectations for attending/presenting, and the process of finding a research advisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make seminar roles, presentation expectations, and advisor selection processes explicit; provide guidance and support for early involvement in departmental seminars and research communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage perseverance while supporting well-being
rubrics_metrics.description: Students emphasized dedication and perseverance ('You have to decide you're going to do it...'); perseverance was described as crucial to success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While fostering perseverance, also provide resources for coping strategies, mental health, and realistic planning so perseverance does not become harmful burnout; help students set sustainable goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support students in redefining measures of success
rubrics_metrics.description: Students needed to adjust their definitions of 'doing well' from undergraduate grade-centered measures to learning and research-centered measures in graduate school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help students recalibrate expectations and notions of achievement (less focus on A grades, more on progress, learning, and research skills) via advising and mentoring conversations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote legitimate peripheral participation (LPP)
rubrics_metrics.description: LPP — engagement in departmental life and the field — encouraged persistence in doctoral mathematics programs by integrating newcomers into communities of practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design departmental activities, apprenticeships, and early research/teaching roles that provide legitimate peripheral participation opportunities so newcomers gain membership and identity within the mathematical community.
